title: Tensor arena reclaim + KV-handle leak investigation causing cross-environment GPU OOMs and fragmentation
creator: Maya Richardson
description: Customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private environments reported repeated GPU OOMs during sustained inference traffic with high session churn. Root cause appears to be a combination of retained KV handles when token-streams are cancelled and suboptimal arena free/coalescing behavior leading to long-tail memory fragmentation on GPUs.
impact: High — production outages and degraded throughput for several customers; increased operational restarts and emergency throttling applied to hosted tiers.
reproduction_steps: 1. Launch an inference workload with 80-120 concurrent sessions, average prompt size 6k tokens, and variable stream cancellations.
2. Randomly cancel 20-30% of active streams mid-generation to exercise abort paths.
3. Monitor per-GPU resident set and arena free lists; observe steadily increasing reserved memory and eventual CUDA OOM after 30-90 minutes.
investigation_summary: Retained KV handles were found in the session slab when requests were cancelled during append; destructor path not always invoked due to async worker scheduling.
Memory fragmentation worsened on Dedicated nodes because we initialize larger per-GPU tensor arenas to favor throughput; coalescing logic was infrequent.
Private on-prem environments exhibited delayed memory release at the driver level (older CUDA drivers), amplifying the visible OOM symptom even after software free paths ran.
temporary_mitigation: Applied per-customer session concurrency caps for the most impacted hosted tenants (rolled out 2026-02-28).
Deployed emergency config to evict idle KV namespaces aggressively (idle_threshold=60s) to recover memory faster.
Scheduled rolling restarts for two dedicated clusters to reclaim fragmented arenas while engineering builds a code fix.
permanent_fix_proposals: Implement eager KV-handle deterministic release on request cancellation to avoid relying on GC/async worker windows.
Add a background arena compactor that coalesces free blocks and returns memory to CUDA in controlled batches.
Introduce fragmentation telemetry and a runtime threshold that triggers conservative model fallbacks (smaller quantized variant) when fragmentation exceeds safe limits.
decisions: Ship combined approach: eager-release + background compactor in the same hotfix to reduce risk of partial fixes.
Conservative default config: compactor interval 5m, compaction window limited to 20% of arena to avoid latency spikes.
Require CUDA >=12.2 for Dedicated and Private recommended builds; Ops to schedule driver upgrades where feasible.
customer_updates: 2026-02-28: Notified AcmeAI of temporary throttling and ongoing investigation (SE + CSM call).
2026-03-01: Bankify provided logs from private runtime showing delayed driver frees; ops coordinating upgrade window.
2026-03-04: Healthlytics approved canary restart window and asked for rollback plan.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - internal reproduce & perf tests (runtime-1.19.2-dev) - complete 2026-03-02
Stage 1 - staging canary (runtime-1.19.2-canary) with synthetic churn workload - 2026-03-03
Stage 2 - Dedicated controlled cohort (2 clusters) with close SLO monitoring - 2026-03-05
Stage 3 - Hosted progressive rollout with traffic shaping and opt-in customers - 2026-03-08
Stage 4 - Private: publish patch package and release notes, coordinate customer upgrades - 2026-03-09
validation_metrics: GPU OOM incidents: target >=90% reduction for patched clusters
KV handle retention time: median <5s after cancellation
Fragmentation index (arena_free_ratio): target decrease to <20% within 10 minutes post-compaction
next_steps: Finish PR feedback loop with kernel team and address concerns about cudaFree on hot path (action: Liu Chen).
Add deterministic integration tests that simulate cancellations and verify KV handle counts (action: QA).
Publish customer-facing release notes and a rollback plan; coordinate with Support and CSMs (action: Maya Richardson).
notes: Kernel team recommended using deferred-free list to avoid synchronously calling cudaFree; compactor drains deferred list under a bounded budget.
Ops observed that certain older NVIDIA driver versions report memory as still in use until process restart; documented in Confluence and flagged as mitigated by driver upgrades.
We may later expose a per-customer compaction aggressiveness knob in Dedicated console if customers require control for latency-sensitive workloads.
